newsitem.title: USA: Fishing boat aground in Rhode Island, fuel spilled.
newsitem.headline: Fishing boat aground in Rhode Island, fuel spilled.

text.p: A 68-foot fishing vessel ran aground earlier in the week in Rhode Island, spilling as much as 5,000 gallons (119 barrels) of diesel fuel into the Atlantic Ocean, U.S. Coast Guard officials said.

The remaining 2,000 gallons (47 barrels) held in the "Green Arrow's" fuel tanks was successfully pumped out in clean-up efforts that followed the Sunday mishap on Block Island, a resort area off the coast of the New England state.
"Yesterday we were able to pump out the remaining fuel. We're guessing most of the fuel went into the environment," Coast Guard Lieutenant Commander Mike Scanlon said Thursday.

He said efforts to minimize the spill's environmental impact through use of an absorbent boom were hurt by waves and by a stiff wind blowing Tuesday on Christmas Eve, which pushed much of the spilled fuel out to sea.
But he noted that mild temperatures in the immediate aftermath of the accident likely helped some of the fuel to evaporate, thereby minimizing environmental damage.
Scanlon also said the steel vessel remained perched Thursday on the rocks that gashed its hull, but that it would soon be removed since no more fuel appears to be leaking.

He noted the pilot of the vessel at the time of the grounding tested positive at the legally established threshold for alcohol intoxication, and that it is possible the U.S. Attorney may press charges against the vessel's owner.
He said the pilot and two others aboard who were sleeping at the time of the incident, were successfully rescued.
"It took some moxie to get them off," he said.
((-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk 1 212 859 1633))
